hypothesis: Wherever a paper pairs a count with a percentage (n / % columns, "n (%)" cells, or "X of Y (Z%)" in text), the percentage must equal 100·n/N within its printed rounding. N is either a denominator the table itself supports (the N most rows agree on, an N stated in caption/footnote/header, or the block's count total) or the explicitly stated Y.
changes: First version. It infers each n/% column pair's denominator robustly from the data and only flags rows that no plausible denominator can explain. It skips weighted tables and row-percentage cross-tabs, and adds an explicit numerator/denominator check for percentages in text.

hypothesis: Parts must reconcile with their wholes and with each other: each percentage must equal count/denominator within rounding; sets of percentages that partition a whole must sum to 100; and a sample size reported in the text must agree with the paper's other statements of that sample size and with the denominators implied by its n/% pairs.

hypothesis: Parts must reconcile with their wholes and with each other. Each percentage must equal count/denominator, where the denominator is shared with the other categories of the same variable. Sets of percentages that partition a whole must sum to 100. A sample size stated in the text must agree with the paper's other statements or implications of that N.
changes: Count/% checking now also infers each variable block's denominator from its other categories, so tables whose blocks have different Ns because of missing data are still checked. The sloppy-paper cap now spans table and text count/% flags combined. Percentage-sum checking now also compares parallel columns, where each column's shares should total 100. Sample-size mentions exclude "n = X, Y%" item counts and approximate values ("approximately 200"), which caused the false alarms.

hypothesis: A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically. That means three things:
changes: Added the bound-containment sub-case (estimate within its CI or range), covering combined "est (lo–hi)" cells, paired lower/upper CI columns, single CI-range columns, Min/Q1/Median/Q3/Max/Mean columns, and "95% CI" statements in text. Removed the sample-size false alarms by ignoring magnitudes like "220 million people" or "226 persons per km²", and by not pairing two explicit mentions in the same paragraph, which usually describe an exclusion step (156 recruited → 150 retained).

hypothesis: A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically. Percentages equal count/denominator, and partitioning percentages sum to 100. Repeated sample sizes agree with each other and with the denominators the paper implies. Point summaries lie within their reported bounds: an estimate inside its CI, and the mean and quartiles inside the min–max with consistent ordering.
changes: Bound checks were missing combined "est (CI)" cells whose header contains "95% CI" because of the "%"-in-header exclusion, so that exclusion now only applies when the header does not mention a CI. Three false-alarm fixes:

hypothesis: A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically:
changes: Added a cross-group additivity sub-case: when a table has a Total/Overall count column and the group counts sum to it in most rows, rows where they do not are flagged. This works even in papers where the count/% check abstains as sloppy. Percentage columns are now also recognised by "Percentage/Percent/Proportion/Share" headers. The sums-to-100 check now also covers category blocks of n/% columns, under a stricter majority rule (at least 3 blocks and 75% of them sum to 100).

hypothesis: A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically:
changes: Count/% discrepancies are now graded. A discrepancy is "strong" when the implied denominator exceeds every plausible N by more than 5% (impossible even with missing data), or when the row is the odd one out in a block of at least two other rows that agree on a denominator shared with the table. Everything else is "weak". Weak discrepancies are still suppressed in papers with more than two count/% discrepancies; strong ones survive, so planted errors in papers with benign missing-data denominators can be caught.

A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically:
changes: The "impossible denominator" route to a strong count/% discrepancy now compares the implied N against the largest N anywhere in the table (all group columns, header and caption Ns), not only the cell's own column. A percentage that could have come from some other plausible group size is now weak. This removes the remaining false alarm in a paper with sloppy group-swapped percentages, while planted errors whose implied N exceeds every N in the table are still flagged.

hypothesis: A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically:
changes: Added the vertical counterpart of the Total-column check. A row labelled Total/Sum/All must equal the sum of the category rows directly above it, column by column. It is flagged only when at least one other count column of that same Total row does reconcile, which shows the row really is a sum of the block. This aims at generalising to unseen accounting mutations; the existing sub-checks are unchanged.

hypothesis: A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically:
changes: The code is identical to version 10. The Total-row check added there had no effect on the visible set (no new hits, no new false alarms), and I keep it because it is the natural vertical counterpart of the Total-column check and may matter on unseen accounting errors. The only remaining false alarm is a paper whose original tables contain genuine count errors, which no rule here can tell apart from planted ones. The remaining misses on the visible set are star and sign flips, which are significance and direction errors, not arithmetic inconsistencies, so they are deliberately left out of scope.

hypothesis: A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically:
changes: The sloppy-paper caps (count/%, cross-sum, bounds) exist only to keep a clean-looking original from being flagged. When the paper already carries at least one uncapped arithmetic flag, it is flagged either way, so the capped discrepancies are now also released. False alarms are counted per paper, so this cannot add new false-alarm papers, but it recovers planted errors in papers that are already flagged.

hypothesis: A paper's reported figures must reconcile arithmetically:
changes: Releasing withheld flags in already-flagged papers neither helped nor hurt on the visible set. It exposed one misfire: the count/% check was applied to a table whose footnote says the percentages are computed "within each level" of the factor (row-level denominators). The count/% check now skips tables whose caption or footnote declares row, within-level or within-category percentages, since the column denominator assumption does not hold there. I keep the release mechanism because it cannot add new false-alarm papers.
